equation.exposition_role: Express the capped two-class earnings allocation.
equation.symbols_units_domain: E,f,c,p,EP,EO are money; n and m are participation units; r is money per ordinary share.
equation.assumptions_timing: Fixed senior entitlement f, nonnegative cap c, n>0, and preference class does not share residual losses.
equation.source_and_equality: p=min(c,m max(E-f,0)/(n+m)); EP=f+p; EO=E-f-p; r=EO/n follow the stated rights.
equation.interpretation: E=0 leaves preference 20 and ordinary -20; E=-40 gives ordinary -60.
equation.transition: Assumed option issuance next changes n and therefore both class allocations.

equation.exposition_role: Represent capped ordinary EPS for the restricted ordering argument.
equation.symbols_units_domain: E,f,c are money, n,m participation populations and each fraction is EPS.
equation.assumptions_timing: E>=f and the stated fixed rights; the following proof additionally assumes additive nonnegative gross earnings and positive shares.
equation.source_and_equality: Subtracting min(c,m(E-f)/(n+m)) from E-f and dividing by n yields max((E-f)/(n+m),(E-f-c)/n).
equation.interpretation: The first branch applies before the cap and the second after it; both share the increment a-rb.
equation.transition: The next-page sign proof justifies ratio ordering only for this restricted family.

equation.exposition_role: Compute earnings and EPS for a complete assumed-conversion set.
equation.symbols_units_domain: P,P(S),B,T,N,H,Ii are money; q,t are rates; n,bi,D are share counts; r is EPS.
equation.assumptions_timing: Shared threshold bonus, proportional complete tax consequence, supplied full-year terms and no participation rights.
equation.source_and_equality: P(S)=P+sum Ii; B=q max(P(S)-H,0); T=t(P(S)-B); N=P(S)-B-T; D=n+sum bi; r=N/D.
equation.interpretation: The common bonus makes earnings nonadditive; at q=0 the after-tax interest effects become additive.
equation.transition: The 80-profit counterexample shows why the lowest world EPS alone is not an admissible selection rule.
